Job Title: Assembler III Reporting To: Operations Supervisor Work Schedule: Onsite – Salt Lake City, UT Moog, Inc. is a global leader in motion control across land, sea air and space, pioneering advanced solutions to drive cutting edge innovation for our valued customers. Job Title: Project Quality Engineer Reporting To: Eng., Project QA Work Schedule: Onsite – Buffalo, NY
Moog is looking for a Project Quality Engineer to plan and execute cost-effective quality processes to assure that we will meet or exceed contractual quality requirements and provide the required level of protection to Moog and its Customers. You will have a measurable impact on the performance of our business by promoting the highest standards of quality. Since the hardware that we produce is very complex, we are looking for someone who understands the important nature of it. You will report to a Project Quality Engineer and work onsite in East Aurora, NY (Buffalo area). Moog Space and Defense (Moog SDG) provides hardware involved in the flow of ignition and systems to the world’s leading space and defense platforms. Headquartered in East Aurora, NY, we employ 13,000 employees in 27 countries. At Moog we have a culture of trust and mutual respect; and for you, working with us can mean deeper job satisfaction, better rewards, and a great quality of life inside and outside of work. To be considered for this role, here’s what you’ll need to bring with you: Bachelor’s degree in engineering or equivalent STEM.
8+ years of professional work experience in Engineering or Manufacturing, 5+ years of which must be in Quality Engineering in manufacturing.
This position requires access to United States export-controlled information.
Proficiency with statistical, spreadsheet, and database software packages
Ability to obtain a US security clearance. As a Project Quality Engineer, you will:
Most importantly, you’ll be relied upon to have integrity, and as someone who won’t be afraid to stand up and say “STOP – we have a problem we that need to address right away.” You may have found that this type of environment hasn’t been encouraged where you’ve worked in the past, but it is here. You’ll have the strength of Moog’s culture behind you to support it.
Develop Engineering professionals to deliver on Moog SDG strategic priorities
Review program and personnel assignments to ensure mission success and equitable work distribution
Be a key stakeholder on program teams in meeting contractual requirements and driving crucial quality related decisions for our customers.
Represent Moog to support Customer & Government (DCMA) inspections, customer audits and requirements.
Improve production by conducting QE studies, recommending design changes, and providing quality support to manufacturing personnel.
Activities will include failure analysis, root cause and corrective action analysis, risk mitigation, material review, customer & governmental interface, audit support configuration control, and traceability.
Review and prepare End Item Data packs to provide to customer during either source inspections or shipment of hardware.
Develop Quality plans for receiving inspection, manufacturing operations, assembly & test processes, and final inspection.
Work directly with customers and suppliers to identify root cause and corrective action.
Improve cost for inspection and prevent cost due to failure through statistical analysis and problem solving. Job Title: Program Administrator Work Schedule: Hybrid – Phoenix, AZ Overview: Program Administrator Experience in contracts and order management with a strong attention to detail and proficiency in ERP systems. Someone who is organized, communicative, and able to coordinate cross-functional teams to meet cost and schedule goals. This role suits candidates aspiring to grow into program management or broader contract responsibilities. The Program Administrator will serve as the key lead liaison between Moog’s contract specialist and program management, providing clear status updates and driving issue resolution. Familiarity with government procurement regulations and space or defense industry logistics is a plus. Comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment, with professionalism and a customer-focused mindset. As a Program Administrator, you will… · Review and manage purchase orders, initiate sales orders, and help coordinate shipping for your assigned space programs; ensure consistency between Moog's proposal, Statement of Work (SOW), and contract requirements, including export-control and mission-unique constraints. · Maintain current, accurate, and traceable contract files, including contract briefs, change logs, and configuration/requirements references required for space missions. · Maintain currency with government and commercial space procurement regulations (e.g., FAR/DFARS as applicable, ITAR/EAR awareness) and escalate compliance questions to Contracts/Legal. · Serve as Moog’s primary point of contact with customers on assigned space programs, providing regular status updates, coordinating technical/ schedule handoffs, and facilitating timely issue resolution for mission milestones. · Develop and manage basic program plans tailored to spacecraft and ground-segment timelines; Here’s what you need to bring with you: · BA degree or a BS degree (Business Administration or a technical discipline is preferred). · Minimum (1+) years of experience in program, project, contract, or production control related responsibilities. · Strong administrative and organizational skills. · Meticulous eye for detail and accuracy. · Ability to multitask and prioritize. · Tact and persistence in dealing with personnel at all levels. Embracing the mindset of “One Moog Team,” the IPT Lead team is committed to leading a team of highly skilled, cross-disciplinary technical professionals, driving the creation of innovative solutions to technical challenges while upholding our commitments to both internal and external customers. The Division IPT Lead is the customer’s primary technical point of contact and is responsible for maintaining the proper balance between the customer’s satisfaction and Moog’s contracted scope of work. The Division IPT Lead is responsible for ensuring the technical compliance of critical system attributes like safety, reliability, performance, and producibility for Moog products in development and/or production in support of a given customer or platform. She/he coordinates the technical interactions between Design and Product Support Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality organizations. These qualities include demonstrating humility, your ability to drive a team to achieve its goals for our division and our customers, and your level of “people smarts” such as mutual trust and respect for others, and providing clear communication to your team, across the functions and management. Prioritize cross-functional collaboration to achieve division and group-level goals. We are all in this together! Support the full lifecycle of the platform, with a heavy emphasis on two areas: (1) ensuring development programs are well-positioned for deterministic execution with technically sound initial assumptions, risk balancing, and structures in place for effective change management; and (2) ensuring production or field quality issues are resolved quickly, in accordance with the terms of the contract(s), and with an eye toward sustaining a positive customer relationship. Job Title: Division IPT Lead Reporting To: Director, ACC Engineering Work Schedule: Hybrid – Tewkesbury, GBR The Division IPT Lead reports to the Commercial Aircraft Deputy Director. It is an over-arching global role with accountability for ensuring the technical and engineering execution performance over the full product lifecycle. Depending on the need, the role is intended to be tailored to provide oversight for either (1) a given customer’s book of business with Moog, or (2) a given platform’s development efforts through NPI phases and into low/full rate production. Embracing the mindset of “One Moog Team,” the IPT Lead team is committed to leading a team of highly skilled, cross-disciplinary technical professionals, driving the creation of innovative solutions to technical challenges while upholding our commitments to both internal and external customers. The IPT Lead is the customer’s primary technical point of contact (TPOC) and is responsible for maintaining the proper balance between the customer’s satisfaction and Moog’s contracted scope of work. The Division IPT Lead is responsible for ensuring the technical compliance of critical system attributes like safety, reliability, performance, and producibility for Moog products in development and/or production in support of a given customer or platform. They coordinate the technical interactions between Design and Product Support Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality organizations. As a Division IPT Lead, you will: Demonstrate the leadership qualities necessary to lead and maintain an effective and cohesive team. These qualities include demonstrating humility, your ability to drive a team to achieve its goals for our division and our customers, and your level of “people smarts” such as mutual trust and respect for others, and providing clear communication to your team, across the functions and management. Demonstrate the charisma, trust, and technical acumen for driving to resolution for complex issues involving engineering, operations, supply chain, quality, programs, and customer considerations. Prioritize cross-functional collaboration to achieve division and group-level goals. We are all in this together! Support the full lifecycle of the platform, with a heavy emphasis on two areas: (1) ensuring development programs are well-positioned for deterministic execution with technically sound initial assumptions, risk balancing, and structures in place for effective change management; and (2) ensuring production or field quality issues are resolved quickly, in accordance with the terms of the contract(s), and with an eye toward sustaining a positive customer relationship. Maintain accountability for the Division IPT Lead is adherence to baselined plans from technical, scope, budget, and schedule perspectives. She/he is also accountable, from a technical perspective, for leading and validating Comprehensive-Estimation-at-Complete (CEAC) activities, variance explanations and Return-to-Green (RTG) planning as needed. Ensure technical solutions and initiatives are fully integrated into functional and division business objectives, priorities, and technology roadmaps, by aligning closely with division and site leadership to assess present and future business needs and direction. Act in full coordination with Functional Engineering, Product Engineering, the Office of Chief Engineers, and Business Unit/Program leadership to ensure New Product Introduction (NPI) efforts are planned and executed successfully, effectively managed through production ramp-up challenges, and sustained through the entire production run. Deliver on the technical, scope, budget, and schedule commitments made to Moog’s Business Sector and its customers for development and production programs. Have a deep understanding of earned value management (EVM) techniques and project management fundamentals like critical path analysis, risk/scope/change management, product cost vs. price, etc. Reduce the potential for product quality issues before they impact a customer, thereby maintaining the customer’s confidence in Moog as a critical partner. Establish relationships with customer and Moog networks built on trust and competence. Maintain good emotional intelligence, deliver clear and transparent communication, and actively listen to the “voice of the customer.” Demonstrate effective “systems thinking” and the ability to understand how technical performance, producibility and product quality, business considerations, and customer needs all must be balanced. Job Title: Senior Reliability Engineer Reporting To: Management, Design Engineering Work Schedule: Hybrid – Wolverhampton, GBR As a Senior Reliability Engineer, you will… Provide technical leadership for reliability and safety engineering activities across complex aerospace development programs, serving as Moog’s reliability authority for systems involving integrated electromechanical, hydraulic, and electronic technologies. Lead and coordinate system‑level reliability and safety analyses, integrating inputs from internal engineering teams and external partners into cohesive, defensible reliability assessments that support certification, program execution, and customer commitments. Develop, tailor, and execute reliability predictions and advanced analytical models to support Reliability and Availability guarantees, helping quantify operational risk, forecast failure and repair activity, and inform proposal and warranty strategies. Perform and oversee a full range of reliability and safety analyses, including: Reliability Prediction
Failure Modes, Effects & Criticality Analysis (FMECA)
Fault Tree Analysis (FTA)
Flight Safety Probability of Loss of Control (PLOC) Analysis
System Safety & Safety Hazard Analysis (SHA)
Common Mode Analysis (CMA)
Physics of Failure (PoF) assessments
Built‑In‑Test (BIT) coverage and system health monitoring architecture development Act as the reliability engineering lead on programs involving system‑level integration of complex hardware, such as motor control electronics, flight control computers, and linear/rotary electromechanical or hydraulic actuation systems. Evaluate reliability and safety requirements to recommend technical strategies, assumptions, ground rules, exceptions, and caveats that ensure compliance while reducing contractual and program risk—particularly in fixed‑price or performance‑guaranteed programs. Define, evaluate, and recommend reliability test strategies, including Reliability Development Growth Testing (RDGT) and other qualification or demonstration approaches, working closely with Environmental and Test Engineering teams to ensure cost‑effective and meaningful results. Develop and refine predictive reliability models—including customized or novel analytical approaches—to forecast field performance, reliability growth, spares demand, repair volumes, and long‑term support implications. Support Moog’s proposal and business‑capture activities by providing statistical forecasts and documented assumptions that inform pricing, spares inventory, test equipment needs, facilities planning, and lifecycle cost exposure. Serve as a trusted technical advisor to design, systems, quality, environmental test, program management, and supply chain teams, ensuring reliability considerations are embedded early and consistently throughout the product lifecycle. Provide technical mentoring and guidance to junior reliability engineers and, where required, support component engineering activities such as component selection, obsolescence management, and technical risk evaluation. Engage directly with customers, certification authorities, and external partners, presenting reliability methodologies, analyses, trade studies, and program risk positions with clarity and technical credibility. To be considered for the Senior Reliability Engineer role, here’s what you’ll need to bring with you: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace Engineering, or a closely related discipline. 5+ years of experience in a Reliability Engineering role supporting complex, safety‑critical systems. Demonstrated experience performing and leading advanced reliability and safety analyses at the system level. Strong understanding of reliability modeling, prediction methodologies, and statistical forecasting techniques. Proven ability to work independently, exercise engineering judgment, and lead technical decisions with minimal supervision. Experience collaborating across multidisciplinary engineering teams and external partners. Strong communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical analyses to technical and non‑technical stakeholders. It would be preferred if you also had: Experience supporting aerospace or other highly regulated, safety‑critical industries. Familiarity with reliability growth, warranty modeling, and availability‑based contractual requirements. Experience influencing program decisions where reliability performance carries commercial or financial risk. Background supporting proposal development, customer negotiations, or performance‑guaranteed programs. Experience mentoring junior engineers or providing technical leadership within a reliability organization.
